title: Every app module that defines a table model ships a packaged migration history
intent: A deployed Terp app builds its schema from packaged migrations, not ``create_all`` (the production boot guard ``assert_migrations_current`` applies them) — so an ``app/modules/<name>`` that declares a ``table=True`` model but has no ``migrations/versions/`` revision would deploy with that table **missing**: the boot guard checks only *declared* histories, so it never notices, and the first request 500s on a nonexistent table. This rule fails the build instead, the build-time complement to the runtime boot guard (the two halves of the migration control). Run ``terp migrate make <name>`` and commit the generated revision.

runtime.rationale: The migration runtime owns the seam but does not yet refuse this rule's core violation: assert_no_homeless_tables fails closed only on an unowned table wired into an owned one by a foreign key (deliberately scoped against fixture false-positives), and the boot guard assert_migrations_current refuses only pending revisions of declared histories. A standalone missing history -- the case this rule exists for -- is visible in the same seam's live metadata but not yet refused, so it is held at build time only.
